title: Deep learning denoises LRO images of lunar permanently shadowed regions
summary: HORUS, a two-stage deep neural network (DestripeNet and PhotonNet), post-processes LRO NAC images of permanently shadowed regions and reveals boulders and craters down to 3 m at about 1.5 m/pixel, with no evidence of surface frost or near-surface ice. It was checked on synthetic data and by cross-comparison of sunlit and shadowed regions and of multiple images. The no-ice finding is an absence of evidence at NAC resolution; an earlier preprint was not checked.
ai_technology: HORUS two-stage deep neural network (DestripeNet and PhotonNet) for image denoising
organization: Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research

evidence.tested: Synthetic-data tests, sunlit versus shadowed cross-comparison and cross-comparison of multiple images.
evidence.unknown: Presence of ice below the resolution limit; any earlier preprint date.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning removed noise and revealed shadowed terrain.
